title: Windows relay login lifecycle
summary: The native Windows relay uses an interactive per-user scheduled task. Sign-out stops it; reboot leaves it unavailable before login; the next login starts it. Desktop lock leaves it running. Battery use does not stop it. Task Scheduler restrictions report the reason and recovery. There is no guaranteed shutdown grace period; durable custody is reconciled at the next start. Setup installs the task for local and HTTPS destinations; relay status shows its identity, enabled state and policy refusal.
